text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Egypt's Holding Company for Food Industries bought 165,000 tonnes of hard red winter wheat and/or hard Australian wheat, seller's option, for July and August shipment. Two 55,000-tonne cargoes for July sold for $168.25 per tonne and 55,000 tonnes for August was at $168.75e.
CORN SALE - USDA said private exporters reported sales of 240,000 tonnes of corn to unknown destinations, of which 30,000 tonnes was for 1996-97 and 210,000 tonnes for 1997-98.

CORN SALE - The Pusan division of South Korea's Korea Feed Association bought 52,500 tonnes of corn from Cargill, traders said. It paid $132.97 a tonne C and F if sourced from the U.S. Gulf, $133.77 a tonne C andF if from the Pacific Northwest or $128.77 a tonne C and F if from China. Shipment was for August 6-25 if sourced from the U.S. Gulf, for August 22-Sept 10 if from the Pacific Northwest or Sept 6-25 if from China.
- The Philippine Association of Feed Millers Inc on Monday bought 55,000 tonnes of No. 2 U.S. yellow corn at $137.75 per tonne C and F, traders said.
CORN AND SOYBEAN SALE - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group bought 38,000 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 of corn from South America for July 16 to August 5 shipment, traders said.

CORN TENDERS - Naseem Agriculture of Abu Dhabi seeks 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine or South African yellow maize for second half August shipment, South Africa's shippers association said. Bids are due June 6.

SOYBEAN TENDER - The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association on Tuesday will seek two 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S., Brazilian or Argentine soybeans for July to September shipment, traders said.

SOYMEAL AND TAPIOCA TENDERS - The South Korean National Livestock Coopeatives Federation will re-invite tenders to buy 40,000 tonnes of soymeal, 52,000 tonnes of feed wheat, 30,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellets and 14,000 tonnes of rapeseed meal on Tuesday after passing last Friday due to higher offer prices.
DURUM TENDER - Algeria was scheduled to tender June 3 to buy 150,000 tonnes of optional durum wheat for shipment in July and August, European grain traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka seeks 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of PL-480 wheat for June 30-July 19 shipment. Offers are due by 1630 GMT June 5 at the Sri Lanka embassy in Washington.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs seeks offers June 4 to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for July with confirmation on June 12.

MARKET TALK - The United States will vote to approve renewal of the Iraqi "oil-for-food" deal, which expires on June 7, a source familiar with the decision said on Monday. Earlier Monday, a State Department spokesman said the Clinton administration would decide later this week whether to support a six-month renewal of the deal, which lets Iraq sell up to $2 billion worth of oil and use the money to buy food and medicine.
